intent: Fix the BokehJS DatePicker (issue #9129) showing the day before the picked date for users in UTC+ timezones by shifting the incoming Date by the browser's timezone offset in DatePickerView._unlocal_date, so the displayed date matches the user-specified date regardless of local timezone. Adds the first Selenium integration tests for DatePicker (label, JS on_change value and displayed text, server round trip).

findings.title: UTC- browsers now show Python-supplied dates, min_date and max_date one day early
findings.suggested_fix: Convert by the representation the model holds instead of shifting every value. Pass the raw model value to _unlocal_date: a number is a UTC-midnight timestamp from Python, so read UTC fields -- new Date(d.getUTCFullYear(), d.getUTCMonth(), d.getUTCDate()); the string written by _on_select (date.toDateString()) parses as local midnight, so read local fields -- new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate()). Checked with node under UTC, Europe/Paris, Asia/Tokyo, Asia/Kolkata, Pacific/Kiritimati, America/Los_Angeles, America/New_York, America/St_Johns and Pacific/Honolulu: both a Python date (Date.UTC(2019,8,20)) and a picked date ('Mon Sep 16 2019') come out on the right day in every zone. Assumptions: _on_select keeps storing toDateString() (per the #4965/#7048 comment), and no caller sets an ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' string, which JavaScript parses as UTC and would need the UTC branch.
findings.why_it_matters: Every user whose browser is west of UTC (all of the Americas) now sees the day before the date Python supplied: DatePicker(value=date(2019, 9, 20), min_date=date(2019, 9, 1)) renders Sep 19 with a lower bound of Aug 31, where the code before this change rendered Sep 20 and Sep 1. The change fixes the reported off-by-one for UTC+ users after a click and introduces one for UTC- users on initial load, on every server-side assignment of value, and permanently on both bounds. The new shift is only right for a value at local midnight, which is what _on_select stores; dates from Python arrive as milliseconds at UTC midnight, so subtracting a positive getTimezoneOffset() moves them into the previous UTC day. Choosing UTC or local fields by the value's type handles both representations in every timezone.
evidence: bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts:68,70,71 -- defaultDate, minDate and maxDate all pass through this._unlocal_date(new Date(this.model.value | min_date | max_date)), so the value and both bounds are affected.

bokeh/util/serialization.py:183-184 -- elif isinstance(obj, dt.date): return (dt.datetime(*obj.timetuple()[:6]) - DT_EPOCH).total_seconds() * 1000 -- Python dates reach BokehJS as milliseconds at UTC midnight (bokeh/core/json_encoder.py:185-186 routes every datetime type through this).
bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts:95 -- this.model.value = date.toDateString() -- the only value at local midnight is the one written after a pick; it is the case the shift fixes.

Executed (node v24, old and new function bodies transcribed, TZ set per run), input Date.UTC(2019,8,20): America/Los_Angeles, America/New_York, America/Sao_Paulo, Pacific/Honolulu -> old 'Fri Sep 20 2019', new 'Thu Sep 19 2019'. UTC, Europe/Paris, Asia/Tokyo, Pacific/Kiritimati -> old and new both 'Fri Sep 20 2019'.

Executed, input 'Mon Sep 16 2019' (a picked value): Europe/Paris, Asia/Tokyo, Pacific/Kiritimati -> old 'Sun Sep 15 2019' (the reported bug), new 'Mon Sep 16 2019'; all UTC- zones and UTC -> old and new both 'Mon Sep 16 2019'. The fix for #9129 itself holds.

Follow-on in a UTC- browser: after a pick, value is converted correctly but min_date and max_date are still Python timestamps and stay one day early on every re-render (date_picker.ts:54 re-renders on any model change). Under standard Pikaday minDate/maxDate behaviour the real max_date day cannot be picked and the day before min_date can; the Pikaday source is not installed in this checkout, so that last step is not quoted.
examples/models/file/widgets.py:66 -- date_picker = DatePicker(value=date(2017, 8, 1)) -- the project's own example renders Jul 31 2017 in a UTC- browser after this change.

residual_risks: A value or bound given as a datetime with a time of day now lands on the viewer's local calendar day instead of the UTC day, so different viewers see different days (reported by the adversarial read: Date.UTC(2019,8,20,23,30) becomes Sep 21 in Europe/Berlin and Asia/Kolkata; the old code gave Sep 20). The new tests pass max_date=datetime.utcnow(), which is such a value. Same root cause as finding 1; reading UTC fields for timestamps removes it.
The effect of the shifted min/max bounds on which days can be picked rests on standard Pikaday behaviour; the pinned Pikaday package is not installed in this checkout and was not read.

Nothing was run in a browser: the project build, npm install and the Selenium suite were unavailable. The conversion logic was checked by transcribing the old and new function bodies into node and running them under nine timezones.
testing_gaps: The three new Selenium tests pass with the fix reverted when the test machine runs in UTC, and cannot see the UTC- regression in any timezone. No timezone is set anywhere in the test setup (none found in bokeh/_testing, the conftest files, or scripts/ci); under UTC getTimezoneOffset() is 0 and the old and new _unlocal_date return the same day for every input (executed with node). Nothing asserts the initially displayed date or the min/max bounds: tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py:43-50 checks only the label, and :68 reads the input text only after a click. Worth adding: an assertion that the input shows 'Fri Sep 20 2019' before any click, and a check of the conversion under at least one UTC+ and one UTC- timezone (a BokehJS unit test of _unlocal_date needs no browser).
